content.text: The quote must be verbatim from one paragraph; let me correct it.

input.quote: 11.2 Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position on every material term: (a) 11.1 gives up to six months of transition assistance at Customer's request, at the rates in the expiring Order Form (more favourable to us than "then-current rates"), expressly including knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier and continued service at existing scope and service levels; (b) 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, and bars withholding over a fee dispute; and (c) 11.3 provides secure deletion with written officer certification. Critically, deletion under 11.3 occurs only "After Customer confirms successful return," so there is no risk of Customer Data being destroyed before we retrieve it, and the legally required retention copy stays protected and use-restricted. Section 10 does not undercut this: 10.1 ends access only after any agreed transition period and preserves our rights in Customer Data, and 10.2 adds Deliverable delivery plus refunds of prepaid Fees. No redline needed.
